topic: Saving state across configuration changes and process death; SharedPreferences and DataStore
title: Notes that survive rotation and process death
instructions:
## Three places data can live

A notes app loses everything when the phone rotates, and again when the system kills the process in the background. Fix both.

## Do this

1. On `Home`: an input `note`, a **Save** button that appends the input to the list `notes`, clears the input and shows a toast "Saved", and a list widget showing `notes`. Refuse to save an empty note (show a toast "Write something first").
2. Set `"retainState": true` on Home so a half-typed note survives rotation (a ViewModel).
3. After saving, **persist** the `notes` key (SharedPreferences), and **load** it in Home's `onCreate` so the notes come back after "Kill process and relaunch".
4. Test every case in the emulator before checking.
hints: Wrap the save in an if: { "action": "if", "input": "note", "notEmpty": true, "then": [...], "else": [{ "action": "toast", "text": "Write something first" }] }
After append: { "action": "persist", "keys": ["notes"] } then { "action": "clear", "id": "note" } and the toast.
"onCreate": [{ "action": "load", "keys": ["notes"] }] on the Home screen restores the list after a kill.

checks.label: Saving a note adds it to the list and clears the input
A half-typed note survives rotation
checks.message: After rotation the input is empty. Set "retainState": true on the Home screen.

checks.label: Saved notes survive a process kill
checks.message: After the kill the list is empty. Persist the notes when saving and load them in onCreate.

realityNote: On Android the three layers are: a ViewModel for configuration changes, onSaveInstanceState for the system killing the activity, and DataStore or Room for anything that must outlive the process. Many real apps lose a user's typing on rotation because they handle only the last one.
